subject: biology
promptStrong: Give me a challenging GCSE exam-style question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the AQA spec.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for GCSE AQA Biology simply, with a worked example and the most common mistake.

questions.q: Which statement correctly describes a prokaryotic cell such as a bacterium?
options: Its genetic material is contained within a nucleus
It is larger than a typical eukaryotic cell
It has no nucleus; DNA is a single loop free in the cytoplasm plus small plasmids
questions.explain: Prokaryotic cells have no true nucleus. Their DNA is a single circular loop in the cytoplasm, often with additional small rings called plasmids. They are also much smaller than eukaryotic cells.

questions.q: Which structure is found in a plant cell but NOT in an animal cell?
questions.explain: Plant cells have a cellulose cell wall (plus a permanent vacuole and often chloroplasts). Ribosomes, mitochondria and the cell membrane are found in both plant and animal cells.

questions.q: What is the function of the mitochondria in a cell?
options: Controls the activities of the cell
Site of most aerobic respiration reactions
questions.explain: Mitochondria are the site of most of the reactions of aerobic respiration, transferring the energy the cell needs. The nucleus controls the cell, ribosomes make proteins, and chloroplasts absorb light.

questions.q: A sperm cell has many mitochondria in its middle section. How does this help it carry out its function?
options: It digests the egg cell membrane
It increases the surface area for diffusion
It stores genetic information for the egg
It releases energy for the tail to swim to the egg
questions.explain: The many mitochondria release energy through aerobic respiration to power the movement of the tail (flagellum), enabling the sperm to swim towards the egg.

questions.q: Root hair cells are adapted for absorbing water and mineral ions because they have:
options: A long thin extension increasing surface area
questions.explain: Root hair cells have a long, thin projection that greatly increases the surface area for absorbing water (by osmosis) and mineral ions (by active transport). They have no chloroplasts as they are underground.

questions.q: What is cell differentiation?
options: The process by which a cell divides into two
The process by which a cell becomes specialised for a particular function
The movement of substances across a membrane
questions.explain: Differentiation is the process by which a cell acquires different sub-cellular structures to become specialised for a specific job. In animals most differentiation happens early in development.

questions.q: Which is an advantage of an electron microscope compared with a light microscope?
options: It is cheaper and easier to use
It shows living specimens in natural colour
It has much higher magnification and resolving power
It cannot be used to study sub-cellular structures
questions.explain: Electron microscopes have much higher magnification and higher resolving power than light microscopes, so they reveal fine detail such as sub-cellular structures. However, they are expensive and cannot view living cells.

questions.q: A cell has a real diameter of 0.05 mm and appears 10 mm wide under a microscope. What is the magnification? (magnification = image size / real size)
questions.explain: Magnification = image size / real size = 10 mm / 0.05 mm = 200, so the magnification is x200. Always convert both measurements to the same units first.

questions.q: During which stage of the cell cycle does the DNA replicate and the number of sub-cellular structures such as mitochondria and ribosomes increase?
questions.explain: Before mitosis, in the first (interphase/growth) stage, the cell grows, DNA replicates to form two copies of each chromosome, and sub-cellular structures increase in number.

questions.q: Two cells produced by mitosis are described as:
options: Genetically identical to each other and to the parent cell
Having half the number of chromosomes
questions.explain: Mitosis produces two genetically identical daughter cells, each with the same number of chromosomes as the parent cell. It is used for growth, repair and asexual reproduction.

questions.q: Mitosis is important for which of the following?
options: Growth and repair of body tissues
Reducing the chromosome number by half
questions.explain: Mitosis produces identical cells for growth, repair and asexual reproduction. Meiosis (not mitosis) produces gametes and reduces the chromosome number by half.

questions.q: What is a stem cell?
options: A cell that can only divide once
An undifferentiated cell able to divide and give rise to many cell types
questions.explain: A stem cell is an undifferentiated cell that can divide by mitosis and differentiate into many other cell types. Embryonic stem cells can form nearly all cell types.

questions.q: In plants, where are stem cells found that allow growth throughout life?
options: In meristem tissue at growing tips of shoots and roots
questions.explain: Plant meristem tissue (found at the tips of shoots and roots) contains cells that can differentiate throughout the plant's life, allowing continued growth and production of clones.

questions.q: Which is a risk or ethical concern with using embryonic stem cells for treatment?
options: Rejection or transfer of viral infection, plus ethical objections to using embryos
questions.explain: Concerns include possible transfer of viral infection, immune rejection, and ethical objections because embryos are destroyed. Therapeutic cloning could reduce rejection because cells carry the patient's genes.

questions.q: Diffusion is best defined as the net movement of particles:
options: Against the concentration gradient using ATP
From a higher to a lower concentration, down a concentration gradient
From a lower to a higher concentration, requiring energy
Only of water across a partially permeable membrane
questions.explain: Diffusion is the net movement of particles from a region of higher concentration to a region of lower concentration (down the gradient). It is passive and needs no energy from respiration.

questions.q: Which factor would INCREASE the rate of diffusion across a cell membrane?
questions.explain: A higher temperature makes particles move faster, increasing the rate of diffusion. A larger surface area, greater concentration difference and shorter distance also increase the rate.

questions.q: Osmosis is the movement of:
options: Water from a concentrated to a dilute solution
Any dissolved solute across a membrane
Water molecules from a dilute to a more concentrated solution through a partially permeable membrane
questions.explain: Osmosis is the diffusion of water molecules across a partially permeable membrane from a dilute solution (high water concentration) to a more concentrated solution (lower water concentration).

questions.q: A piece of potato is placed in pure water. What happens to its mass?
options: It increases as water enters the cells by osmosis
It decreases as water leaves the cells
It decreases as solute enters the cells
questions.explain: Pure water is more dilute than the potato cell contents, so water moves into the cells by osmosis, increasing the potato's mass. In a concentrated solution the potato would lose mass.

questions.q: How does active transport differ from diffusion?
options: It moves substances against the concentration gradient and requires energy from respiration
It moves substances down the concentration gradient without energy
questions.explain: Active transport moves substances against the concentration gradient (from low to high concentration) and requires energy transferred by respiration. This is how roots absorb mineral ions and the gut absorbs sugars.

questions.q: Why do large multicellular organisms need specialised exchange surfaces and transport systems?
options: Their surface area to volume ratio is too small for diffusion alone to supply all cells
Diffusion is faster in large organisms
questions.explain: As organisms get larger their surface area to volume ratio decreases, so diffusion across the outer surface is too slow to supply every cell. They need exchange surfaces (e.g. lungs) and transport systems (e.g. blood).
